title: Islamic Umm al-Qura Calendar
intro: Umm al-Qura is a published-table-style Hijri calendar associated with Saudi civil dating.
structure: The twelve month lengths are 29 or 30 days according to the maintained year table, rather than a universal alternating rule.
model: The provider supports AH 1300–1600 inclusive, from the first day of 1300 to the final day of 1600. The data contains retrospective dates; conversion uses maintained month lengths and rejects dates beyond the table without extrapolation.
example: Ramadan AH 1447 can be calculated using the stored month table. AH 1700 is unsupported and must not produce an invented date.
history: Published month tables support consistent scheduling and recordkeeping. Other Islamic authorities may choose different dates using local sightings or other conventions.
limits: Not a universal religious determination or proof of a historical crescent observation. No dates outside the maintained table are supported.
